x: This duel ended suddenly after the fourth lap when Gebbett and Black drew away to a comfortable lead having run their rivals into the ground.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.
The field set off at a fair pace and a check on positions at 5 miles found E. Gebbett 9th, R.

As a complete result did not appear in the last issue of the magazine, we take the liberty of supplying the missing details. In addition to Collis, Gebbett and Plummer whose positions and times were given, the following members completed the course:- 44th.
Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.

Jack Brown was lying about 36th with Eric Gebbett leading the rest of the team in about 120th position. A course of this nature however, called for restraint in the early stages, when many spent too much energy endeavouring to move up before they had even allowed the field to settle down.

It was however, a Belgrave best and was only 12 sec. outside the stage record held by none other than Ken Norris. 5th Eric Gebbett Eric continued the good work through Redhill and quickly passed Poly to take us into fourth place.

Eric Gebbett's turn came next on the long undulating leg from Handcross to "The Castle" at Hickstead. This leg is generally reserved for the best runners of each club, and our difficulty, in recent years, has been to find someone of sufficient calibre to keep on equal terms with other teams.

Only Baulch and Gebbett ran true to form and finished in positions which deserve any special mention. Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.
Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th.
Eric Gebbett was, as usual, quickly in the lead and he, together with Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch, took the field along at a very brisk pace.
However,on leaving the Common for Copse Hill Pat was way ahead and increasing his lead with every stride; the role of pack leader being taken over by Eric Gebbett.
Let the individual positions speak for themselves - Newell 59th, Shippen 136th, Baulch 158th, Gebbett 174th, Bedford 205th and Walker 248th.

Newly married Eric Gebbett, whose current running form was unknown, ran very well in his first race for some time, but Woodford in the shape of Eric Major (13:10) swept past both ourselves and T.V.H., to take third position.
Jack Brown was 21st, Charlie Dabbs (without shoes, à la Tulloh) 32nd, Masters 47th, Dooley 57th, Gebbett(recovering from gastric trouble) 60th and Johnston 64th.
